description: A brace that holds a statement is not a one-expression brace: in `.B :> { one(); 2 }` the bare `2` is a second item and owes its `;` (E-STMT-MISSING-SEMICOLON, once). In this value position it is also E-ARM-TAIL-VALUE, the ruling's code for a bare tail after a statement: after a statement the arm yields only by `lift`. (With the `;` it is E-ARM-TAIL-VALUE alone.)
provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S469 "⭐ RULED — `{ e }` in a value-position match arm is that expression" — "Allow { e } in arms too (Recommended)" ("`lift` is required once the block holds a statement, and a bare tail after a statement is E-ARM-TAIL-VALUE") · ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S469 "⭐⭐⭐ RULED — dpa-073 F1 = (a)" — `;` terminates
rationale: §7.2.2 rule 3 (S474): a brace that holds a statement or a second item is a statement list, and rule 1 applies to each statement. §18.5: a bare tail after a statement in a value position is E-ARM-TAIL-VALUE (the ruling's code), pinned on its own by match-block/s474-arm-tail-value-after-statement. impl#1 does not enforce `;` (dpa-073 F5: a carried, impl#1-labelled divergence, g-dpa063-termination-unbuilt-impl1-legacy — the xfail gap here), and it does not emit E-ARM-TAIL-VALUE either (g-impl1-arm-tail-value-unemitted-s474); the bootstrap emits both.
